draft.title: Human wellbeing
card: Human wellbeing is the quality of people's lives. It is about how well people are living, not only how much money they have.
It has many parts, including health, education, income, safety, freedom and a clean environment.
The parts can differ from person to person and place to place. A person can have a high income but live with polluted air, so one part is strong and another is weak.
Geographers look at all the parts together to judge how well people in a place are living.
draft.remember: Wellbeing is the quality of people's lives, and income is only one part of it.

a.q: Which statement best describes human wellbeing?
opts: The quality of people's lives, across many parts
The total amount of money people earn in a place
The number of people who live in a place
How much of a place's land is used for farming
a.why: Wellbeing covers how well people live, including health, education, safety and a clean environment. Income is tempting, but it is only one part of wellbeing and does not describe all of it.
a.clue: Wellbeing is about more than one thing.

b.q: Wei lives in a city in Australia and earns a high wage. His suburb has very polluted air that often makes him unwell. What does this show about his wellbeing?
opts: Some parts of it are strong and others are weak
His wellbeing is high because his income is high
His wellbeing is low because he lives in a city
Pollution is not part of human wellbeing
b.why: Wellbeing has many parts. Wei's income is strong, but a clean environment and health are weak, so the parts differ. High income alone does not make wellbeing high, because it is only one part.
b.clue: Look at each part of Wei's life separately.

a.best: The quality of people's lives, across many parts

b.best: Some parts of it are strong and others are weak
